brief_title: Oxxynea Supplementation for Gut Comfort in GLP-1-Based Therapy Users
official_title: A Randomized, Triple-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Effects of a Supplement on Gut Comfort in GLP-1-Based Therapy Users

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in GIQLI Gastrointestinal Symptoms domain score

brief_summary: This virtual, two-arm, randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated whether daily supplementation with Oxxynea, a polyphenol-rich botanical blend, improves gastrointestinal comfort in adults using GLP-1-based therapies who experience gastrointestinal symptoms and report low fruit and vegetable intake. Participants took one capsule daily with the first meal of the day for six weeks and completed questionnaires at home.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male or female, aged 18-65 years
* BMI \>= 27 kg/m2
* Currently taking a GLP-1-based therapy (GLP-1 receptor agonist or dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist)
* At least two of the following since starting GLP-1 therapy, at least 2-3 times per week: gut discomfort, diarrhea, abdominal pain/cramping, bloating, nausea
* Self-reported low fruit and vegetable intake (less than 2 pieces per day)
* Generally healthy (no uncontrolled chronic disease)
* If taking supplements/herbal remedies for gut comfort, stable for \>= 3 months and willing to maintain them
* Resides in the United States
* Willing to follow the protocol and maintain diet, sleep and activity levels

Exclusion Criteria:

* Chronic conditions preventing protocol adherence, including oncological and psychiatric disorders
* Antibiotic use in the last 15 days
* Planned introduction of new products, medications or supplements targeting gut comfort
* History of severe digestive disorders (e.g., acid reflux, celiac disease, IBS, IBD, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease) or GI surgery
* Allergy or sensitivity to any study product ingredient; known sulphite sensitivity
* Pregnant, breastfeeding or trying to conceive
* Anticoagulant use or bleeding disorder
* Medications that may interact with botanical supplements (e.g., antihypertensives, glucose-lowering agents, antiplatelets, grapefruit-interacting drugs)
* Serious illness in the last 3 months or planned surgery during the study
* History of substance abuse; heavy alcohol use; current smoker or smoked in the past 3 months
* Participation in another research study
* Chronic hepatic or renal disease
